decision: Reject H-only proposal for current layout; defer tile-local proposal as incomplete. Retain checkpoint recomputation as a separately costed hypothesis, not an implementation recommendation.
corrections: We do not checkpoint every mixed-add intermediate point. Only final C,Y,W,ZZZ state and inverse product-tree nodes cross the kernel boundary. H-only per-step output does not replace these values or reconstruct recovery without more information/work.

A tile-local tree plus a global root hierarchy already describes our current decomposition. Shared memory cannot remain live across the separate prepare, root-inverse and finish launches; the proposal does not supply a valid persistence/recomputation/synchronization plan.
The referenced OpenCL example performs inversion within a workgroup; it does not demonstrate eliminating checkpoints while preserving our one-inversion-per-large-batch architecture.

The cited paper full HTML is available. Sections3.2–3.3 describe grouped inversion, recomputation of inexpensive intermediates and cache placement; they do not establish a zero-global-checkpoint variant for this source.

A concrete recomputation variant would remove254 field-node stores+loads per256 candidates but add254 multiplications and up-sweep barriers in finish. It retains128B/candidate recovery state. At477182283/s removed checkpoint payload is30.3GB/s; no measured bottleneck or substantial gain follows.
feedback: For future memory proposals identify the exact current stored symbol, byte count, use and lifetime before proposing removal. Explain kernel-boundary synchronization and reconstruction. A bibliography of batch inversion methods is not itself a new mechanism.
